# Extension views

An extension view is a GUI that an extension describes once, as data. The extension mounts the view with `ctx.ui.mountView`, and every client attached to the session draws it with its own controls: the terminal draws rows, and a web page draws HTML. A view is a tree of nodes (text, lists, inputs, buttons), the intents a user can raise, and optionally alternatives for different clients and a drawing. A view fills a slot such as a panel, a widget row or a dialog. No client runs extension code.

> **Differs from Pi (D614).** Pi has no views. Pi's `ctx.ui.custom` components draw in the terminal only. Stock PiG attaches no view client, so `ctx.ui.viewAbilities()` returns `null` and `ctx.ui.mountView` rejects with code `unsupported` until a Piglet attaches one.

This page uses the Node SDK, because a `.mjs` extension loads without a build. [The calls in each SDK](#the-calls-in-each-sdk) names the same calls for Go, Python, Rust and Lisp.

## Try it

The terminal draws views when the active Piglet sets `viewClient: terminal`. Save this Piglet next to the extension file and start it with `pig --piglet ./views.yaml`.

```yaml
name: views
description: "Draw extension views in the terminal and serve them to other clients."
viewClient: terminal
viewEndpoint: socket
extensions:
  - name: todo
    origins:
      - local:./todo.mjs
```

A Piglet's `extensions` and the `-e` option load a `.mjs` file. The extensions folders load only `.ts` and `.js` files ([Extensions](extensions.md)).

After you edit the extension, type `/reload`. A reload ends the mounts of the old instance and the new instance mounts again.

`viewEndpoint: socket` serves the session's views on the Unix socket `<agent directory>/view-endpoint/<pid>.sock`, for example under `~/.pig/agent/view-endpoint/`. A client program of the same user attaches there. The `pig` binary contains no web page and no web server. The reference web client is in the PiG repository, in `examples/ui-view-web`, and needs Node:

```bash
node examples/ui-view-web/bridge.mjs --connect ~/.pig/agent/view-endpoint
node examples/ui-view-web/bridge.mjs -- -e ./todo.mjs
```

The first command attaches a web page to the running terminal session. The second command starts a `pig` of its own for each page and needs no Piglet. Both print the page's address, `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/?token=<token>`.

## A complete extension

This extension mounts a todo list in the `panel` slot. A terminal draws the plain view. A web page draws the alternative.

```js
// todo.mjs: one todo list for the terminal and a web page.
export default function todo(pi) {
  const items = [
    { id: "milk", label: "Buy milk", done: false },
    { id: "letter", label: "Send the letter", done: true },
    { id: "plants", label: "Water the plants", done: false },
  ];
  let mount = null;

  const open = () => items.filter((item) => !item.done).length;
  const list = () => ({
    kind: "select-list",
    id: "items",
    items: items.map((item) => ({ value: item.id, label: `${item.done ? "[x]" : "[ ]"} ${item.label}` })),
  });
  const clear = { kind: "mouse-region", id: "clear", region: { types: ["press"] }, children: [{ kind: "text", text: "[ Clear done ]" }] };
  const plain = () => ({ root: { kind: "vstack", children: [{ kind: "text", text: `Todo: ${open()} open` }, list(), clear] } });
  const rich = () => ({
    root: {
      kind: "vstack",
      gap: 1,
      children: [{ kind: "markdown", text: `# Todo\n\n**${open()}** of ${items.length} open.` }, { kind: "hstack", gap: 2, children: [list(), clear] }],
    },
  });
  const content = () => ({
    view: plain(),
    alternatives: [{ when: { any: [{ all: [{ claim: "client.kind", op: "equals", value: "web" }] }] }, view: rich() }],
    intents: [
      { name: "todo.toggle", nodeKey: "items", arg: { type: "object", properties: { value: { type: "string" } }, required: ["value"] } },
      { name: "todo.clear", nodeKey: "clear", arg: { type: "object" }, answer: { type: "object", properties: { removed: { type: "integer" } }, required: ["removed"] } },
    ],
    a11y: [{ node: "items", name: "Todo items", role: "list" }, { node: "clear", name: "Clear done items", role: "button" }],
    focus: [{ node: "items", request: "mount" }, { node: "clear" }],
    fallback: { kind: "text", text: "The todo list does not fit this client." },
  });

  // Mount once, when a client that draws panels is attached.
  const show = async (abilities, ctx) => {
    if (!abilities || mount || !abilities.slots.includes("panel")) return;
    mount = (await ctx.ui.mountView({ key: "todo", slot: "panel", ...content() })).mount;
  };
  pi.onViewAbilities(show);
  pi.on("session_start", (_event, ctx) => show(ctx.ui.viewAbilities(), ctx));

  pi.onViewIntent(async (inv, ctx) => {
    let answer;
    if (inv.intent === "todo.toggle") {
      const item = items.find((entry) => entry.id === inv.arg.value);
      if (!item) return { outcome: "refused", error: "no such item" };
      item.done = !item.done;
    } else if (inv.intent === "todo.clear") {
      const before = items.length;
      items.splice(0, items.length, ...items.filter((item) => !item.done));
      answer = { removed: before - items.length };
    } else return { outcome: "refused", error: "unknown intent" };
    mount = (await ctx.ui.updateView(mount, content())).mount;
    return { outcome: "done", answer };
  });
}
```

## Mount, update and end

- `ctx.ui.viewAbilities()` returns what the attached clients draw, or `null` when no client is attached. The record has `slots`, `nodes`, `markdown`, `imageFormats`, `limits`, `input`, `claims`, `slotClaims` and `drawing`. With several clients it is their merge.
- `pi.onViewAbilities((abilities, ctx) => ...)` runs when the first client attaches, when the abilities change and when the last client leaves (`null`). It does not run for the state the extension starts in, so also read `ctx.ui.viewAbilities()` at `session_start`.
- `ctx.ui.mountView({ key, slot, view, intents, alternatives, drawing, a11y, focus, fallback })` mounts the view and resolves to `{ mount, state }`. `key` is 1 to 128 bytes and names the mount inside your extension. `view` is `{ root: node }`. Only `key`, `slot` and `view` are required. The slots `tool-card`, `message` and `entry` also need `target: { toolCallId }`, `{ messageType }` or `{ entryType }`.
- `mount` is the ref `{ key, epoch, rev }`. Every operation returns a new ref. Pass the newest ref to the next operation: an older ref fails with code `stale`.
- `ctx.ui.updateView(mount, content)` replaces the whole content. `content` has the members of a mount without `key`, `slot` and `target`.
- `ctx.ui.hideView(mount)` and `ctx.ui.showView(mount)` hide and show a mount without ending it.
- `ctx.ui.finishView(mount, result)` ends a mount as completed, and `result` is any JSON value of at most 65536 bytes. `ctx.ui.removeView(mount)` ends it as withdrawn. After either, an operation on the mount fails with code `terminal`, and you can mount the same key again.
- `ctx.ui.viewState(key)` returns `{ mount, state, reason, result }`. `state` is `live`, `hidden`, `finished`, `removed` or `broken`. The host breaks a mount with `reason` `session_replaced`, `owner_gone` or `shutdown`.
- `ctx.ui.viewDiagnostics(key)` returns the notices of a mount: which update the host rejected, which intent it ended, and what a client did not draw. The host keeps 32 notices for a mount.
- `/reload` loads the extension as a new instance. The mounts of the old instance are `broken` with reason `owner_gone`. The new instance holds no mount and mounts again.

## Nodes

A node is a JSON object with a `kind`. Give a node an `id` when an intent, an `a11y` record, a `focus` record or a drawing names it. A kind that the client does not list in `abilities.nodes` rejects the mount with code `invalid`. Sizes are terminal cells.

| Kind | What it is | Members |
|---|---|---|
| `vstack`, `hstack` | children in a column or a row | `children`, `gap`; a child's `stack: { basis, grow, shrink, minSize, maxSize }` |
| `container` | children in a column, without padding | `children` |
| `box` | padded children on a background | `children`, `paddingX`, `paddingY`, `bg` |
| `text` | wrapped text | `text`, `paddingX`, `paddingY`, `bg` |
| `truncated-text` | one row of text, cut at the width | `text` |
| `markdown` | rendered markdown | `text`, `defaultTextStyle: { color, bgColor, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough }` |
| `lines` | rows that your extension drew, shown verbatim | `content` (an array of strings) |
| `spacer` | empty rows | `lines` |
| `dynamic-border` | a horizontal rule | `color` |
| `select-list` | a list with one highlighted item; the user chooses an item | `items: [{ value, label, description }]`, `selectedIndex`, `maxVisible` |
| `settings-list` | settings that step through their values | `items: [{ id, label, currentValue, values }]` |
| `input` | one line of text; Enter submits | `value`, `placeholder` |
| `editor` | several lines of text | `value` |
| `mouse-region` | one child that a click activates; use it as a button | `children` (one node), `region: { types: ["press"] }` |
| `scroll-view` | one child that scrolls | `children` (one node), `follow: "end"` |

A `bg`, a `color` and the colors of a `defaultTextStyle` name theme tokens ([Themes](themes.md)).

## Intents

An intent is an action that the user raises on a mount. Declare every intent in `intents`:

```js
const intents = [
  { name: "todo.toggle", nodeKey: "items", arg: { type: "object", properties: { value: { type: "string" } }, required: ["value"] } },
  { name: "todo.close", arg: { type: "object" }, cancellable: true, timeoutMs: 5000 },
];
```

- `name` is `<extension>.<verb>`. A name is declared once in a mount.
- `nodeKey` binds the intent to the node with that `id`. Choosing a `select-list` item, changing a `settings-list` value, submitting an `input` or an `editor`, and clicking a `mouse-region` raise the intent.
- `arg` is the shape of the argument. The host checks the argument against it before your handler runs. Declare `{ value }` as a string for a `select-list` (the item's `value`), an `input` and an `editor` (the text). Declare `{ item, value }` for a `settings-list` (the setting's `id` and its new value). Declare `{ type: "object" }` for a `mouse-region`.
- A shape is `{ type }` with `boolean`, `string`, `integer`, `number`, `enum` (`enum`: at most 32 strings), `object` (`properties`, `required`; at most 32 properties, no other member is accepted) or `array` (`items`, `maxItems`; at most 64 items). A shape nests at most 4 deep.
- `answer` is the optional shape of the handler's answer. `timeoutMs` is 100 to 300000 and defaults to 30000. `cancellable: true` lets the host abort `inv.signal` at the timeout.
- An intent without `nodeKey` belongs to the whole mount. A client decides how to offer it.

One handler answers every intent: `pi.onViewIntent(async (inv, ctx) => ...)`. `inv` has `intent`, `arg`, `nodeKey`, `mount`, `rev`, `ticket` and `signal`. Return `{ outcome: "done", answer }`, `{ outcome: "refused", error }` or `{ outcome: "failed", error }`. Change your state, call `ctx.ui.updateView` through the handler's `ctx`, wait for it, then answer. The client is sent the new view before it is told that the intent is done. An update from outside the handler while it answers settles the intent `stale`.

## Alternatives

A client states facts about itself as claims. `alternatives` (at most 8) gives a client another view when its claims match. The host sends each client the first alternative whose `when` holds, otherwise `view`. One mount and one state serve every client.

| Client | Claims |
|---|---|
| terminal | `client.kind` = `"terminal"`, `size.columns` (integer), and for each slot `size.rows` (integer) |
| reference web page | `client.kind` = `"web"` |

`when` is `{ any: [{ all: [clause, ...] }, ...] }`: it holds when every clause of one group holds. A `when` has at most 8 groups of 8 clauses. A clause is `{ claim, op, value }`:

| `op` | Holds when |
|---|---|
| `present` | the client states the claim (no `value`) |
| `equals` | the claim equals `value` (a boolean, an integer or a string) |
| `contains` | the claimed list holds every string of `value` |
| `atLeast` | the claimed integer is at least `value` |

```js
const web = { any: [{ all: [{ claim: "client.kind", op: "equals", value: "web" }] }] };
const wideTerminal = { any: [{ all: [{ claim: "client.kind", op: "equals", value: "terminal" }, { claim: "size.columns", op: "atLeast", value: 100 }] }] };
```

An alternative is `{ when, view, drawing }`. It shares the mount's `intents`, `a11y` and `focus`, so use the same node ids in every view. A client is sent the `a11y` and `focus` entries of the nodes that its view has.

## Accessibility and focus

- `a11y: [{ node, name, description, role, selected, checked, expanded, busy, disabled, readOnly, required, invalid, relations }]` describes the node with id `node`. `role` is one of `alert`, `button`, `checkbox`, `dialog`, `group`, `heading`, `image`, `link`, `list`, `listitem`, `menu`, `menuitem`, `progressbar`, `radio`, `region`, `status`, `switch`, `tab`, `tablist`, `tabpanel`, `textbox`, `toolbar`, `tree` and `treeitem`. A relation is `{ kind, target }` with `labelledBy`, `describedBy`, `controls` or `owns`.
- `focus: [{ node, request: "mount", restore: "previous" | "self" }]` makes nodes focusable. The order of the entries is the focus order. At most one entry requests the focus.
- Each list has at most 256 entries. A `node` that no view of the mount has rejects the mount with code `invalid`.

## Drawings

A drawing adds vector shapes or a pixel grid to a view. Send a drawing only when `abilities.drawing.profiles` lists its profile: without a client that draws the profile, the mount fails with code `unsupported`.

```js
// meter.mjs: a level meter. A client that draws the scene profile is sent a drawing. Every other client is sent text.
export default function meter(pi) {
  let level = 3;
  let mount = null;
  let scene = false;

  const raise = { kind: "mouse-region", id: "raise", region: { types: ["press"] }, children: [{ kind: "text", text: "[ Raise ]" }] };
  const drawing = () => ({
    profile: "scene",
    node: "canvas",
    viewport: { x: 0, y: 0, width: 100, height: 20, fit: "contain" },
    shapes: [
      { kind: "rect", x: 0, y: 0, width: 100, height: 20, radius: 4, fill: "#20242c" },
      { kind: "rect", key: "bar", x: 0, y: 0, width: level * 10, height: 20, radius: 4, fill: "accent" },
      { kind: "text", x: 50, y: 14, size: 10, align: "center", text: `${level * 10}%`, fill: "#ffffff" },
    ],
    regions: [{ key: "bar", shape: { kind: "rect", x: 0, y: 0, width: 100, height: 20 }, gestures: ["activate"], intent: "meter.raise", name: "Raise the level" }],
  });
  const content = () => ({
    view: { root: { kind: "vstack", children: [scene ? { kind: "box", id: "canvas" } : { kind: "text", text: `Level ${level} of 10` }, raise] } },
    drawing: scene ? drawing() : undefined,
    intents: [{ name: "meter.raise", nodeKey: "raise", arg: { type: "object" }, answer: { type: "object", properties: { level: { type: "integer" } }, required: ["level"] } }],
    fallback: { kind: "text", text: `Level ${level} of 10` },
  });

  const show = async (abilities, ctx) => {
    if (!abilities || mount || !abilities.slots.includes("panel")) return;
    scene = abilities.drawing?.profiles.includes("scene") ?? false;
    try {
      mount = (await ctx.ui.mountView({ key: "meter", slot: "panel", ...content() })).mount;
    } catch (err) {
      ctx.ui.notify(`meter: ${err.code ?? err.message}`, "error");
    }
  };
  pi.onViewAbilities(show);
  pi.on("session_start", (_event, ctx) => show(ctx.ui.viewAbilities(), ctx));

  pi.onViewIntent(async (inv, ctx) => {
    if (inv.intent !== "meter.raise") return { outcome: "refused", error: "unknown intent" };
    level = Math.min(10, level + 1);
    mount = (await ctx.ui.updateView(mount, content())).mount;
    return { outcome: "done", answer: { level } };
  });
}
```

- `profile` is `scene` (with `shapes`) or `pixels` (with `pixels: { width, height, asset, scaling: "nearest" | "smooth" }` over an image asset declared in `assets`).
- `node` is the id of the view node that the drawing fills. Without `node`, the drawing follows the view.
- `viewport: { x, y, width, height, fit }` is the rectangle of drawing coordinates that the client shows. `fit` is `contain`, `cover` or `stretch`.
- A shape has a `kind` and the members of that kind. A member of another kind rejects the drawing.

| Shape | Members |
|---|---|
| `rect` | `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `radius` |
| `ellipse` | `cx`, `cy`, `rx`, `ry` |
| `line` | `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2` |
| `polyline` | `points: [{ x, y }]` (2 to 1024), `closed` |
| `path` | `commands: [{ op, ... }]` (1 to 1024, the first is `move`); `op` is `move` or `line` (`x`, `y`), `quad` (`x1`, `y1`, `x`, `y`), `cubic` (`x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2`, `x`, `y`) or `close` |
| `text` | `x`, `y`, `text`, `size`, `align: "start" | "center" | "end"` |
| `image` | `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `asset` |
| `group` | `children` |

- Every shape also takes `key`, `fill`, `stroke: { color, width }`, `opacity` and `transform` (six numbers). A color is `#rrggbb`, `#rrggbbaa` or a theme color token.
- `regions: [{ key, shape, gestures, intent, name, role }]` turns a gesture inside `shape` into a declared intent. `shape` is a `rect`, an `ellipse` or a closed `polyline`. A gesture is `activate`, `press`, `release` or `drag`. `name` is required. The client tests which region a pointer is in, and it raises the intent with an argument of the intent's `arg` shape.
- A drawing has at most 4096 shapes nested 8 deep, 1048576 pixels and 64 regions, and never more shapes or pixels than `abilities.drawing.shapes` and `abilities.drawing.pixels` (code `limit`).
- An alternative can carry its own `drawing`. With several clients attached, a client that cannot draw the content it is sent receives the `fallback`, marked `degraded`.

## Slots

`slot` is one of `notify`, `status`, `widget-above`, `widget-below`, `header`, `footer`, `dialog`, `overlay`, `panel`, `tool-card`, `message` and `entry`. A mount has one slot. To show the same state in a panel and in a dialog, make two mounts with two keys. Mount only in a slot that `abilities.slots` lists: another slot fails with code `unsupported`.

## Errors and bounds

A rejected call throws an `Error` whose `code` is one of:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `invalid` | The record is malformed or past a bound of the host: an unknown member, node kind, slot or operator, a key that is already mounted, or a list that is too long. Nothing changes. |
| `unsupported` | No attached client can draw the mount: no client is attached, no client draws the slot or the drawing profile, or the mount declares intents and the client delivers no input. |
| `limit` | The content exceeds what the client states in `abilities.limits` (`nodes`, `depth`, `snapshotBytes`, `textBytes`, `mounts`) or in `abilities.drawing`. |
| `stale` | The ref is not the newest ref of the mount. |
| `terminal` | The mount has ended. |
| `not_found` | The extension has no mount under this key. |

## The calls in each SDK

Every SDK has every call, and its mount takes the same members (`intents`, `alternatives`, `drawing`, `a11y`, `focus`, `fallback`). The Go, Python and Rust SDKs build the `view` with their component kit.

| Call | Node | Go | Python | Rust | Lisp |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| read the abilities | `ctx.ui.viewAbilities()` | `ctx.ViewAbilities()` | `ctx.view_abilities()` | `ctx.view_abilities()` | `ctx-view-abilities` |
| abilities changed | `pi.onViewAbilities` | `ext.OnViewAbilities` | `ext.on_view_abilities` | `ext.on_view_abilities` | `on-view-abilities` |
| mount | `ctx.ui.mountView` | `ctx.MountView` | `ctx.mount_view` | `ctx.mount_view` | `ctx-mount-view` |
| update | `ctx.ui.updateView` | `ctx.UpdateView` | `ctx.update_view` | `ctx.update_view` | `ctx-update-view` |
| hide, show | `hideView`, `showView` | `HideView`, `ShowView` | `hide_view`, `show_view` | `hide_view`, `show_view` | `ctx-hide-view`, `ctx-show-view` |
| finish | `finishView(mount, result)` | `FinishView`, `FinishViewWith` | `finish_view(mount, result=...)` | `finish_view`, `finish_view_with` | `ctx-finish-view` (`:result`) |
| remove | `removeView` | `RemoveView` | `remove_view` | `remove_view` | `ctx-remove-view` |
| state | `viewState` | `ViewState` | `view_state` | `view_state` | `ctx-view-state` |
| diagnostics | `viewDiagnostics` | `ViewDiagnostics` | `view_diagnostics` | `view_diagnostics` | `ctx-view-diagnostics` |
| answer intents | `pi.onViewIntent` | `ext.OnViewIntent` | `ext.on_view_intent` | `ext.on_view_intent` | `on-view-intent` |

## What the clients draw

| Capability | Terminal (`viewClient: terminal`) | Reference web page (`examples/ui-view-web`) |
|---|---|---|
| Slots | `widget-above` and `widget-below` (at most 10 rows each), `panel` (at most half the terminal's rows); every other slot is not drawn at this version | all twelve slots |
| Node kinds | every kind of [Nodes](#nodes) | every kind of [Nodes](#nodes) |
| Limits of one mount | 512 nodes, depth 16, 262144 snapshot bytes, 65536 text bytes, 16 mounts, 4096 intent argument bytes | 2048 nodes, depth 32, 1048576 snapshot bytes, 65536 text bytes, 32 mounts, 65536 intent argument bytes |
| Intents with `nodeKey` | raised by the keys and clicks of the node | raised by the keys and clicks of the node |
| Intents without `nodeKey` | no control | a control on the mount |
| Focus | F6 moves the focus to a panel, Escape returns it to the editor | the `focus` order is the tab order |
| `a11y` | not drawn at this version | `name`, `description`, `role`, the states and the relations become ARIA attributes |
| Drawings | not drawn at this version | not drawn at this version |

[Terminal UI](https://pi-in-go.dev/docs/latest/tui#extension-views) lists the terminal's rows and keys. [Piglets](https://pi-in-go.dev/docs/latest/piglets#view-client) describes `viewClient` and `viewEndpoint`.
